rationale: NWNH sold MSIP as a competed line to keep moderate-scale ground innovation flowing at about $40M per year; the line exists and its awards produced real science (HERA's record 21 cm limits, ZTF's time-domain survey, instrument and design work for the next big projects), which is what the recommendation was for, but at about half the recommended funding and with awards an order of magnitude below the ~$100M top of the intended range, so Astro2020 judged it underfunded: partial.

value: no LISA data: ESA adopted the mission January 2024 for a 2035 launch, NASA hardware contribution a formal project; meanwhile NANOGrav 15-year data (67 pulsars) found Hellings-Downs correlations with a Bayes factor above 10^14, amplitude 2.4 (+0.7 -0.6) x 10^-15 at 1/yr, consistent with a population of supermassive black-hole binaries (2023); LISA's band (10^4 to 10^7 solar mass mergers, Galactic compact binaries) untouched
rationale: NWNH sold LISA on measuring full waveforms from 10^4 to 10^7 solar mass black hole mergers and a census of Galactic compact binaries for a mid-2020s launch; the mission is now a 2035 ESA-led launch with no data, so building. Meanwhile pulsar timing arrays answered a neighbouring question in 2023 by detecting a nanohertz background consistent with supermassive black-hole binaries, but LISA's millihertz band and individual merger waveforms remain unmeasured.

value: no GMT data: GMT first light mid-2030s (GMagAO-X final design, arXiv:2608.10212), NSF construction share zero, TMT dropped; meanwhile JWST spectroscopically confirmed galaxies at z=14.32 and z=13.90, showing 'luminous galaxies were already in place 300 million years after the Big Bang and are more common than expected' (Carniani 2024, Nature 633, 318); the GSMT follow-up (masses, chemical buildup of these galaxies) has no instrument yet
rationale: NWNH sold the GSMT on spectroscopy of the distant galaxies JWST would find and direct imaging of exoplanets, with science from the mid-2020s; GMT is under construction on partner money with first light a decade late, so building. JWST has meanwhile done the discovery half itself, finding unexpectedly luminous galaxies at z of 14, which sharpens the question the GSMT was sold on rather than answering it.

value: US never joined CTAO; CTAO-South first telescopes expected to observe from 2026, initial configuration has no US SCTs (arXiv:2509.05527); meanwhile the combined Fermi-LAT, HAWC, H.E.S.S., MAGIC and VERITAS dwarf-galaxy search (2025) sets 95% limits on <sigma v> of 1.5x10^-24 to 3.2x10^-25 cm^3 s^-1 at 2 TeV (tau tau), 5 GeV to 100 TeV, 2 to 3 times tighter than any one instrument, no detection; CTA is projected to probe thermal-relic TeV dark matter from the Galactic centre (arXiv:2007.16129)
rationale: NWNH sold ACTA on a 10x more sensitive array to detect or constrain annihilating dark matter via gamma rays in the early 2020s; CTAO exists without the US and starts southern observations in 2026, so on the facility it is building, and the dark matter question is still open with existing instruments only pushing limits. Marked guess because on US terms (no US share ever delivered) the row could be read as no, matching the cost-schedule call; the science question itself is unanswered by anyone.
